content:
As of last week we have a sorry-free proof that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation property. This question had been open for quite a while, and the literature was a bit messy, with three previous attempts (Leivant 1981, Borzechowski 1988 and Kowalski 2002) claiming a solution but then later being criticized or revoked. The Lean proof now formalizes our paper (submitted / under review) which in turn is based on the 1988 attempt by Manfred Borzechowski. In fact, we developed the Lean proof in parallel to the paper and Lean has turned me into an annoying nitpicky co-author.

There are bigger things being announced these days, but this project was my original motivation to learn Lean and it feels very good that our paper now will most probably not join the list of revoked attempts for this problem :slight_smile: I thank many others who have been working on various parts of this project in the last three years, including @Madeleine Gignoux @Noam Cohen @Haitian Wang @Wietse Bosman @Xiaoshuang Yang @Amos Nicodemus @Andrés Goens. In the last few weeks also Aristotle AI helped substantially, including some larger refactoring. Last not least, I want to use this chance to thank the community here for all the help!

For the future, I hope to still clean up and shorten the code (currently 33k lines, down from 36k recently), and in the long run I would like to contribute at least the definition of PDL to the modal logic section of Cslib.
